items.stem: What is AI, in plain terms?

options.A: Software that learns patterns from many examples
options.B: A human mind living inside a computer
options.C: A perfect encyclopedia that never errs

items.stem: When an AI writes a fluent answer, what is it mainly doing?

options.A: Checking every fact on the live web first
options.C: Predicting likely next words from patterns it learned

options.B: AI can be useful without thinking like a person

items.stem: How is a simple calculator different from most modern AI?

options.A: A calculator follows fixed math steps; AI leans on learned patterns
options.B: A calculator has feelings; AI does not
options.C: They work in exactly the same way

items.stem: A colleague says "the AI knows the answer." What is a safer way to say that?

options.A: The AI has personal memories of your company
options.B: The AI is conscious and careful
options.C: The AI is producing wording that often fits similar requests

options.A: A tool that can draft text or sort patterns
options.B: A person with goals, beliefs, and life experience
options.C: Software people can use at work

items.stem: Why can an AI sound confident and still be wrong?

options.A: Smooth wording comes from patterns, not from checked truth
options.B: It always double-checks with a human first
options.C: Confidence means it looked the fact up

items.stem: During the AI's practice phase, what does it mainly learn from?

options.B: Magic rules no one can describe
options.C: Many examples of text, images, or other data

items.stem: You should treat an AI answer as:

options.B: A helpful draft you still need to judge
